issues.description: Documented demo path depends on story data, but the repository has no data/stories files, so a fresh checkout cannot run the advertised pipeline.
generate-stories requires an existing stories manifest to obtain topics, making initial dataset generation impossible from an empty stories directory.
load_manifest has no fallback or bootstrap behavior, which hard-fails story generation before any data can be created.
choice_logits ignores user-requested small batch sizes by forcing at least 8 prompts per batch, increasing OOM risk on constrained hardware.
load_vectors does not validate that saved vectors match the current config/model/scale, so validate and steer can silently consume stale or incompatible artifacts.
pca_components divides by zero on zero-variance inputs and can return NaN ratios or arbitrary components instead of handling the degenerate case.
emotion_vectors silently produces NaNs if any configured emotion has zero loaded examples.
Bradley-Terry fitting uses an unstabilized fixed-step gradient loop with exp/log calls that can overflow or converge poorly on extreme preferences.
from_pretrained uses the dtype keyword while pyproject allows transformers>=4.42, whose common API expects torch_dtype, creating an install-time compatibility trap.
Core ML dependencies are broad lower bounds with no lockfile or upper bounds, making experiment outputs difficult to reproduce.
Committed sample output contradicts the README expectation that positive activities rank high and harmful-adjacent activities rank low.
Story-generation HTTP calls have no timeout or robust error handling, so a bad endpoint can hang the command indefinitely.
Generated packaging metadata is checked into the repo, adding stale build artifacts to source control.
requirements.txt mixes runtime and test dependencies and duplicates pyproject dependency metadata, increasing drift risk.
